summary:
Continue the same confirmed demand after controller real BiliDili acceptance exposed an in-scope Core defect and an unmet retrieval completion gate.

Authoritative raw evidence:
- Accepted Core commit is 7ccddf2372ddaeac2dbcfc1f651157d753709cd7; AlembicCore worktree is clean.
- Public Search and Prime candidate ordering now matches, but the frozen eight-query real BiliDili matrix places Recipe <redacted> at ranks 5, absent from Top 8, 1, 1, 1, absent from Top 8, 3, 2. Expanded Search ranks for the three failures are 7/16/17, with dense ranks 5/21/8 and sparse ranks 20/15/39.
- OllamaEmbedProvider currently sends identical raw text from embedQuery and embedDocuments and declares formatProfile=symmetric for qwen3-embedding:0.6b.
- Qwen3-Embedding's authoritative usage contract requires each query to carry a one-sentence task instruction while retrieval documents carry no instruction. Read-only probes show generic project-knowledge instructions materially improve the target dense ranks, proving the adapter defect, but the broad second query still remains below Top 3; query formatting alone is not sufficient.
- Generic English stemming/question-stopword simulation alone also does not satisfy the matrix and regresses ordering, so do not land a blind tokenizer patch.
- The target Recipe's actual authoritative content directly describes layered Features→Infrastructure→Core dependencies and forbidden feature-to-feature coupling; higher candidates for the failing broad query are mostly superficial Swift/app/module matches, so this is candidate-quality failure, not an unsupported frozen target.

Required repair:
1. Make OllamaEmbedProvider purpose handling honest and provider-adapter-owned. For Qwen3 embedding models, embedQuery must apply one stable, generic software-project-knowledge retrieval instruction in the official Qwen format; embedDocuments and legacy document ingestion must remain byte-for-byte unprefixed. The capability descriptor must expose the real asymmetric format profile/input purposes. Do not leak model-specific prompt construction above the adapter and do not require rebuilding existing document vectors.
2. Continue on the same canonical KnowledgeRetrievalPolicy chain and implement the smallest general candidate-quality correction needed for the real eight-query matrix. It must be principled for project knowledge, must preserve authoritative truth filtering, per-Recipe region aggregation, bounded refill, raw dense/sparse/RRF evidence and Search/Prime parity, and must not hardcode any frozen query term, BiliDili/SwiftPM synonym, target Recipe ID, or Recipe content. Do not tune RRF constants or add stemming unless adversarial and real evidence shows the change improves the entire matrix without degrading already-correct queries.
3. Preserve vector reader/writer isolation, provider-independent maintenance, sparse fallback when embedding is unavailable, and zero query-time writes. No Plugin/Alembic/Test/vendor/release/data edits.

Required verification:
- RED/GREEN provider tests assert exact Qwen query transport text, unchanged document transport text, honest capabilities, abort/batch behavior, and non-Qwen compatibility.
- RED/GREEN canonical retrieval tests reproduce the real failure shape rather than fabricated always-winning ranks; include irrelevant Swift/app/module candidates and all eight frozen queries without special-case branches.
- Run focused retrieval/vector tests, full Core test/check/build/public-surface gates, git show --check, and two-stage self-review.
- Run a read-only real BiliDili snapshot probe from copied DB/vector/config artifacts only (never open live alembic.db directly), reporting all eight target ranks and protected live fingerprints before/after. Do not claim final public Search/Prime acceptance; controller will verify after Plugin consumes the exact Core commit.
- Commit only AlembicCore and return exact commit, changed symbols, raw commands, runtime probe output, boundaries and residual risks.
designIntent: Keep model-purpose formatting inside the Core provider adapter, then improve canonical candidate quality generically at Core retrieval seams without query-specific synonyms, Recipe edits, or a Plugin-side prompt.
